prose: The New York Times examines Alpha School, a network of private schools claiming its AI-driven model teaches children twice as fast as traditional schools. According to the Times' analysis of the network's own data, roughly half of K-8 students missed that two-times goal in math. The full reporting, including parent perspectives, is behind the Times' bot protection.
highlights: Alpha School claims AI-driven teaching lets kids learn 2x as fast as traditional schools.
New York Times analysis: about 50% of K-8 students missed that 2x goal in math.
The piece draws on the network's own data and parent accounts; full text unavailable here.
